text:
incident-bot: PAGE: Sev2 — Elevated 5xx and latency from eu-west-2. Alert summary: 5xx rate 9.4% over 5m, p95 latency 2.3s, error spike started ~2m ago. Pager: @maya-oncall

maya-oncall: saw it. first glance - spike aligns with increased traffic to provider 'fastnet-eu' pools.

tom-sre: confirm, getting similar in the runtime dashboards. KV cache miss rates up, token generation retries also rising.

priya-platform: any deploys in eu in last 30m? I'm not seeing infra pushes.

deploy-bot: deploys: none in last 60m.

raj-netops: traceroute shows intermittent packet loss to fastnet-eu edge nodes: 
```
PING fastnet-eu-1 (10.14.2.7): 100 packets transmitted, 12 packets lost, rtt min/avg/max = 4.2/28.1/300 ms
```

maya-oncall: OK, plan: 1) quick partial brownout (disable non-critical features for eu-west-2) 2) apply conservative rate-limits for free-tier / low-priority routes 3) start provider reroute of 40% traffic to backup provider 'steelflow' 4) notify CS for customer comms.

emily-cs: copying. Need an impact blurb asap — I'll ping customers on seats > $10k if this expands.

nate-eng: what routes are non-critical? suggestion: disable streaming for embeddings and low-QPS debug endpoints.

priya-platform: I'll push a change to the routing policy. Drafting command: 
```
rdrctl routing override --region eu-west-2 --route-group noncritical --action disable --reason "provider instability"
```

maya-oncall: +1. Do safe rollout, 10% -> 30% -> 100% if metrics OK.

tom-sre: I'll coordinate the rate-limit. Proposed qps throttles: free-tier global -> 5r/s per client, trial accounts -> 2r/s, enterprise unchanged. Command: 
```
platform-admin rate-limit set --region eu-west-2 --profile free --qps 5
platform-admin rate-limit set --region eu-west-2 --profile trial --qps 2
```

raj-netops: starting provider reroute job to steer 40% from fastnet-eu -> steelflow. Using throttled cutover to avoid oscillation. Command: 
```
rdrctl provider reroute --from fastnet-eu --to steelflow-eu --region eu-west-2 --percent 40 --staged 10,20,40 --watch metrics
```

incident-bot: ACTION LOG -> maya-oncall initiated routing override 1m ago.

maya-oncall: executing step 1 (non-critical feature brownout) now — rolling 10% of service nodes. Monitoring.

10m later...

tom-sre: after brownout and 40% reroute: 5xx rate down to 3.1% and p95 to 860ms. Good signal. Need to keep an eye on steelflow error profile (different failures seen).

priya-platform: ramping reroute to 60% over next 5m per plan.

raj-netops: note: fastnet-eu still has packet loss spikes, but traffic shaping + reroute reduced downstream pressure.

emily-cs: initial customer impact note: ~12% of requests affected during peak window, most were non-critical and from free/trial customers. Premium customers saw degraded latency for ~8 minutes. I'm sending proactive note to paid customers impacted.

nate-eng: we should also enable local KV prefills to reduce cold misses while provider is unstable. Patching config: 
```
serving-config set --region eu-west-2 --kv-prefill true --prefill-size 50
```

maya-oncall: good call. Doing that now.

incident-bot: MONITOR -> p95 latency trending down, error rate trending down. Next action window in 15m.

priya-platform: reroute now at 60%. Observability shows steelflow error rate slightly elevated (0.8%), but overall lower 5xx than before.

tom-sre: starting a partial capacity drain of fastnet-backed pools to avoid sudden failover during later ops. Command: 
```
rdrctl drain-provider-pool --provider fastnet-eu --region eu-west-2 --target 25% --grace 120s
```

raj-netops: applied. Draining 25% now, will observe connection churn.

maya-oncall: summary for post-incident report draft: root cause suspected transient network flapping on fastnet-eu causing KV cache pressure + retries. Mitigation: brownout non-critical features, rate limits on low-tier accounts, staged reroute to steelflow, partial drain of fastnet pools, KV prefill. Current status: Stable, 5xx ~1.6%, p95 520ms.

emily-cs: sending customer note to 3 mid-market accounts who reported errors. Template: "We experienced elevated errors and latency in eu-west-2 today. Actions taken: routing changes and rate limits to protect critical services. If you saw impact, contact us at support@redwood.ai" — ok to send?

maya-oncall: send. Add "we prioritized premium traffic and rolled out fixes within 20m"

nate-eng: quick follow: logging shows a persistent retry loop in the tokenizer service when upstream latency >200ms. We should add early abort at 1s to avoid cascading load. Filing a follow-up issue.

tom-sre: agree — mark as postmortem action item.

maya-oncall: handing on-call to @tom-sre for continued watch and postmortem ownership. I will be available for context.

tom-sre: ack, taking over. Will keep the reroute at 60% for now and keep drains in place until fastnet shows stable packet loss <1% for 30m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE -> Status: mitigated (partial). Severity: Sev2. Owner: tom-sre. Summary note posted to #incidents-log.

emily-cs: thanks team. I'll follow up with affected customers and update the support tickets.

maya-oncall: good job everyone. Closing the active paging window. We'll do a brief async postmortem in ~1h to capture timeline and action items.
